name: Akroma's Will
oracle_text:
Choose one. If you control a commander as you cast this spell, you may choose both instead.
• Creatures you control gain flying, vigilance, and double strike until end of turn.
• Creatures you control gain lifelink, indestructible, and protection from each color until end of turn.
blocked_sentences: Choose one. If you control a commander as you cast this spell, you may choose both instead.

needs.what: `Game._ask_modes` must read `up_to_if` the way it already reads `all_if`. Rule 601.2b picks modes as the spell goes on the stack, so a spell whose whole effect tree holds one top-level `choose_mode` never reaches `op_choose_mode`'s mode question at all -- `CardDef.cast_time_modes` hands the spec to `Game._ask_modes`, which answers it during the cast and records the answer on the stack item. That method computes `count`, applies `all_if`, and calls `ask_mode(ctx, "Choose", labels, pid, max(1, count))` with no `up_to` argument. The `up_to_if` branch shipped in `op_choose_mode` is unreachable for exactly this shape of card. Four lines mirroring the `all_if` block would close it, and the timing lands right for free: `_ask_modes` runs *as the spell is cast*, which is where the printed condition "as you cast this spell" is measured -- whereas `op_choose_mode` evaluates it at resolution, one priority window too late.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Measured, not guessed. With the card written as `{"op": "choose_mode", "count": 1, "up_to_if": {"condition": {"exists": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "is_commander": true}}, "count": 2}, "modes": [...]}` it passes all six gates, and it is still the wrong card: with a commander on the battlefield the `CHOOSE_MODE` decision is built `min=1 max=1`, so both modes are never offered. Burying the `choose_mode` inside an `if` so `top_level_mode_spec` cannot see it does produce `min=1 max=2` and both modes resolve -- which proves `up_to_if`, `grant_protection` and the condition are all correct and isolates the fault to the cast-time path -- but it is a deformation of the card to dodge the engine: it moves a 601.2b choice to resolution, hides it from opponents holding responses, and wraps the spell in an `if` whose condition means nothing. Shipping either is a modal that always chooses one mode, which is a different card.

needs.what: The loader should guard `up_to_if` the way it guards `all_if`: refuse it on any op that is not `choose_mode`, and run `validate_condition` over `up_to_if.condition` and `validate_value` over `up_to_if.count`. Secondary to the need above, and the same class of bug -- `loader.py` was not touched when `up_to_if` shipped.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: There is no validation of `up_to_if` anywhere, so a misspelling, a malformed condition, or the key placed on the wrong op all load perfectly cleanly and are silently ignored. That is precisely the failure the `all_if` guard exists to prevent -- 'a card that reads "choose both" and chooses one' -- and it is what made the blocker above invisible: the card compiles, plays, and clears gate 5 while its first printed sentence does nothing.

notes: Both needs the previous record named are shipped and were checked here. The second bullet is fully expressible: `grant_keyword` for lifelink and indestructible plus `{"op": "grant_protection", "from_colors": ["W","U","B","R","G"], ...}` gives every creature you control `protection_from` == {W,U,B,R,G}, verified on the board. Only the choose-one line is still blocked.

"If you control a commander as you cast this spell" needs nothing new -- `{"exists": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "is_commander": true}}` says it exactly, and it discriminates correctly: false with no commander, false with a commander in the command zone, true with one on the battlefield.

`{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"commander_color_identity": "you"}, "right": {"const": 1}}` is NOT that sentence and should not be used. `commander_color_identity` unions the *printed* colour identity of every commander a player has, deliberately regardless of zone -- its docstring says so, because War Room wants a deck-construction fact. Measured in the sandbox: with a commander sitting in the command zone and nothing on the battlefield it returns 2, so the condition fires when the player controls no commander at all. It also returns 0 for a colourless commander on the battlefield, so it fails to fire when they do. Wrong in both directions; no narrower value is needed, because `exists` + `is_commander` already says it.
